name: Neck-Shoulder Tension (Severe)
description: 4-phase program for severe tension: Gentle relaxation, careful mobilization, light strengthening, maintenance - significantly reduced dosage
pain_rule: Only perform exercises at pain <= 3/10. Immediately reduce load at any increase in tension. Relaxation always takes priority.
evidence_base: Gross et al. (2015): Exercise for mechanical neck disorders
Jull et al. (2008): Cranio-cervical flexion training
Falla et al. (2012): Specific deep cervical flexor exercise
Ylinen et al. (2003): Active neck muscle training in chronic neck pain
Cramer et al. (2013): Yoga for chronic neck pain
progression_criteria: Phase 1 -> 2: 21 days, min. 5 sessions, tension significantly reduced, sleep improved
Phase 2 -> 3: 21 days, min. 5 sessions, good mobility, pain <= 2/10
Phase 3 -> 4: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, strength built up, pain <= 3/10

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Deep Relaxation**

With severe tension, your nervous system is overstimulated. The most important step now is: relaxation. We start very gently and give your body the time it needs.

**Goal:** Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension.

**Strategy:**
- Extensive breathing exercises as the foundation
- Minimal repetition count for all exercises
- Extra long stretch positions (60 seconds)
- Stay in this phase for at least 21 days
- If worsening: only breathing exercise and stretching

**Scientific Basis:** With severe tension, calming the nervous system is more important than mechanical exercises. Breathing exercises activate the parasympathetic nervous system and reduce baseline muscle tension (Cramer et al., 2013).
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Careful Mobilization**

Your baseline tension has decreased - a great success! Now we carefully begin with mobility and control. Every exercise remains gentle and pain-free.

**Goal:** Build initial mobility and control.

**Strategy:**
- Very careful progression
- Greatly reduced repetition counts
- Relaxation exercises remain part of every session
- No resistance band resistance in this phase
- If setbacks: return to Phase 1 exercises

**Scientific Basis:** Gradual load progression with high symptom levels prevents exacerbations and promotes confidence in one's own resilience (Falla et al., 2012).
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Light Strengthening**

You have already achieved a lot! Now we begin with gentle strengthening - exclusively with bodyweight and minimal resistance.

**Goal:** Build basic strength without overloading.

**Strategy:**
- Only bodyweight and lightest band resistance
- Few repetitions, long rest periods
- Relaxation exercise before and after training
- If tension increases: immediately halve intensity

**Scientific Basis:** Even minimal strengthening improves postural control and reduces tension long-term. The dosage must be individually adapted (Ylinen et al., 2003).
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Maintenance & Prevention**

You have come a long way! In this phase, it is about maintaining what you have achieved and preventing relapses. Relaxation remains a central component.

**Goal:** Long-term freedom from symptoms with a relaxation-focused maintenance program.

**Strategy:**
- Maintain daily relaxation routine
- Regular micro-breaks at the workplace
- Self-massage as a fixed routine
- Light maintenance training 3x/week
- During stress periods: intensify relaxation

**Scientific Basis:** For patients with severe tension tendency, a long-term relaxation program is the most important predictor for recurrence-free outcomes.

exercises.name: Deep Diaphragmatic Breathing with Body Scan
exercises.description: Lying on your back, legs bent. Hands on your abdomen. Breathe deeply through the nose into the belly (4 sec), exhale slowly through the mouth (8 sec). While exhaling, mentally scan through the body: forehead, jaw, neck, shoulders, arms - consciously release everything. Minimal repetitions, maximum mindfulness.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Gentle Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Lying on your back with a pillow under the head. Very gently retract the chin - minimal range of motion is enough. Lengthen the neck. Hold position only briefly, then fully relax. No forcing.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Minimal Cervical Mobility
exercises.description: Lying on your back or seated upright. Move head minimally (50% of pain-free range) in each direction: forward, backward, left, right. Extremely slow and deliberate. Stop immediately at any discomfort.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Long Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.description: Sit upright. Right hand grips under the chair. Very gently tilt head to the left - only by gravity, NO hand pressure on the head. Feel the gentlest stretch. Hold 60 seconds. Switch sides. Breathe calmly and deeply throughout.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Gentle Scapular Control
exercises.description: Lying on your back, arms loosely beside the body. Very gently press shoulder blades toward the floor and minimal retraction. Hold position only briefly, then fully release and relax.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Long Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description: Sit upright. Slightly rotate the head to the left, then gently tilt forward and down. Right hand grips under the chair. Stretch only by gravity, do not assist. Hold 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and calmly throughout. Switch sides.
exercises.phase_goal: Calm the nervous system and reduce baseline tension

exercises.name: Gentle CCF Endurance
exercises.description: Lying on your back, head on a pillow. Very gently and minimally tuck the chin. Carefully increase hold time to 6-8 seconds. At any effort or tension, release immediately. Relaxation breathing between repetitions.

exercises.name: Prone Y/T/W (Minimal)
exercises.description: Lying face down. Lift arms only a few centimeters off the floor in Y-, T-, and W-position. Gently squeeze shoulder blades together. Hold only 1 second, lower. No effort - only activation.

exercises.name: Wall Slides (Reduced)
exercises.description: Stand with your back against the wall. Place arms in 90-degree position against the wall. Slide arms only a few centimeters upward - reduced range of motion. Stop immediately at pulling or tension.
exercises.intensity: Very light - minimal range of motion

exercises.name: Gentle Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description: Side-lying, knees bent. Open the top arm only partially to the other side - 50% of possible range of motion. Do not force end range. Hold 2 seconds, gently return.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation (No Weight)
exercises.description: Side-lying, top arm at the body, elbow bent 90 degrees. Slowly and gently rotate the forearm upward. No weight. Minimal range of motion is enough. Elbow stays at the body.

exercises.name: Relaxation Breathing (Session Start)
exercises.description: Every training session begins with relaxation breathing. Lying on your back, close eyes. Inhale 4 seconds, exhale 8 seconds. Consciously relax shoulders, jaw, forehead. Only begin exercises once baseline tension has been lowered.

exercises.name: Neck Flexor Activation
exercises.description: Lying on your back. Tuck the chin and lift the head only minimally (a few millimeters) off the surface. Hold only 5 seconds. Immediately lower if trembling occurs. Quality above all.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrugs without Weight
exercises.description: Standing, arms hanging loosely. Slowly (3 sec) raise shoulders upward, briefly hold at the top, lower for 3 seconds in a controlled manner. Bodyweight only - no added weight. Fully relax between repetitions.

exercises.name: Band Face Pulls (Lightest Resistance)
exercises.description: Attach lightest resistance band at face height. Gently pull band toward the ears. Minimal resistance. Squeeze shoulder blades together. Very slowly return. If tension arises: stop exercise.

exercises.name: Prone I/Y/T (Bodyweight)
exercises.description: Lying face down. Gently lift arms in I-, Y-, and T-position off the floor. No added weight. Only lightly squeeze shoulder blades together. Hold 1-2 seconds, lower, briefly relax.

exercises.name: Gentle Isometrics (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Place hand against the head: front, back, left, right. Head holds position against LIGHT hand resistance. Only 30% of maximum force. 6 seconds per direction. Build force very slowly and release very slowly.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up (Gentle)
exercises.description: Stand arm's length from the wall. Hands shoulder-width on the wall. Slowly lean toward the wall, push back in a controlled manner. At the top, gently push shoulder blades forward. Very light load.

exercises.name: Relaxation Breathing (Before and After Training)
exercises.description: Every training session begins AND ends with relaxation breathing. Lying on your back, close eyes. Inhale 4 seconds, exhale 8 seconds. Consciously release shoulders and neck. Essential with severe tension.

exercises.name: Workplace Micro-Break (Relaxation Focus)
exercises.description: At the desk every 30-45 minutes: 1) 3 deep breaths with shoulder relaxation, 2) Gentle chin tuck (3 sec), 3) Shoulder circles (3x). Shorter intervals than with milder tension. Relaxation takes priority.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms with relaxation focus

exercises.name: Daily Self-Massage
exercises.description: Fixed daily routine: 1) Stroke the upper trapezius with fingers (3 min), 2) Work suboccipital muscles at the base of the skull with circular movements (2 min), 3) Gently massage jaw and temple muscles (2 min), 4) Shoulder-neck junction with tennis ball against the wall (3 min).
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms with relaxation focus

exercises.name: Evening Relaxation Routine
exercises.description: Daily evening routine (10 min): 1) Lying on your back, legs bent, 2) 5 min deep belly breathing with body awareness, 3) Gentle upper trap stretch 60 sec per side, 4) Gentle levator stretch 60 sec per side. Helps with sleep problems caused by tension.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms with relaxation focus

exercises.name: Gentle Maintenance Circuit
exercises.description: Adapted circuit (3x/week): 1) Relaxation breathing 4x, 2) Chin tuck 5x, 3) Gentle shoulder shrugs 5x, 4) Wall slides 5x, 5) Upper trap stretch 60s per side. 60 sec rest between exercises. 1 round is enough.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms with relaxation focus

exercises.name: Long-Term Maintenance Program
exercises.description: Weekly program for after the protocol: Mon/Wed/Fri: Gentle maintenance circuit (10 min), Daily: Self-massage (10 min) + Evening relaxation (10 min), At workplace: Micro-breaks every 30-45 min. During stress periods: double the relaxation.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms with relaxation focus
